record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: Which broad and mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds can be described explicitly? Here an affine Poisson manifold means a finite-dimensional manifold equipped with an affine atlas and a Poisson bi-vector P whose Schouten self-bracket [[P,P]] vanishes.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Describe ample classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds (M^r_aff, P).

artifact.self_contained_problem: An affine Poisson manifold is a pair $(M, P)$ where $M$ is a finite-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with an affine atlas (i.e. a maximal atlas whose chart transition maps are affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^{\dim M}$), and $P \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ is a bi-vector field on $M$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P, P]\!] = 0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Equivalently, the bracket $\{f, g\} := P(df, dg)$ on $C^\infty(M)$ is a Poisson bracket.\n\nProblem. Identify and explicitly describe broad, mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds $(M, P)$. That is, exhibit families of such pairs (for instance, characterized by the form of $P$ in affine coordinates, by symmetry, by the structure of the symplectic foliation, or by other geometric/algebraic properties) which are sufficiently large and natural to serve as a useful supply of examples, and give explicit normal forms or classifications within each class.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research question asking for a description of broad classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds. No comprehensive classification or solution appears in the literature; it remains an open-ended descriptive problem.
